BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our internal playbook, and the Seller's update and Disclosure Letter as received

---

## 0. Threshold points before the clause-by-clause review

**1. The "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim has no effect on our side.**
The Seller's preamble says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." Nothing in our authority process confirms this. Amelia Frost has given no written authority for any fallback. Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, a counterparty's statement that something is agreed, final or pre-cleared is an assertion, not an instruction. We should treat every position below as open. If anyone on our side believes something was agreed at principal level, they should confirm it with Amelia Frost in writing before we rely on it.

**2. "Market standard" is not a basis for concession.**
The claimed ranges (10–20% caps, roughly 1% baskets, 12–18 month periods, buyer-knowledge qualifiers) are the Seller's characterisation. We negotiate from our playbook, not from their market survey.

**3. The Seller's cover note contradicts its own Disclosure Letter.**
This is the most useful leverage point. The cover note presents several matters as resolved or immaterial. The Disclosure Letter, which is the document with legal effect, says otherwise:

| Matter | Cover note says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | No final consent; no evidence conditions satisfied (§2) |
| Riverlark | release post-Completion | Not repaid; no discharge (§3) |
| Bonuses | "matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed (§5) |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification duty all unknown; investigation preliminary (§6) |
| Sandbar | "ordinary-course" | Disclosure does not state whether ordinary course, terminable or accrued (§8) |
| Title | evidenced by DD-012 | DD-012 is the source relied on; Buyer has not verified (§10) |

**4. The facts are stale.**
The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. We should request an updated, dated status on Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and Sandbar. We should separate any verified updates (documents, bank confirmations) from assertions.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap: Clause 12.1 (Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m)
- **Departure:** Our position is 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Why push back:** 20% is our conditional fallback. It may only be used with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. No such authority exists. A Seller proposal that happens to match our fallback number is not cleared for that reason (playbook 6.3).
- **Action:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal any flexibility. If the team wants to consider 20%, escalate to Amelia Frost with this draft identified, and treat it as tied to wins elsewhere (fundamentals, fraud, disclosure, knowledge), not as a standalone concession.

### 1.2 Thresholds: Clause 12.2 (Seller: AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket)
- **Departure:**
  - De minimis is 5x ours (AUD 5k).
  - Basket is 5x ours (AUD 50k).
  - The Seller's basket is a deductible ("only the excess"), whereas ours is a tipping basket (first dollar once exceeded).
- **Why it matters:** Together these could absorb a significant volume of real claims. A run of AUD 20k claims would never count, and the first AUD 250k of eligible loss would be lost permanently.
- **Action:** Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping. The playbook contains no authorised fallback here.

### 1.3 Time limits: Clause 12.3 / 13 (Seller: 18 months, plus a blanket "applies to all Claims")
- **Departure:** Our position is 24 months. 18 months requires Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Hidden override:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would quietly sweep title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general regime. This breaches our rule that these categories stay separate.
- **Action:** Restore 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the blanket language and replace it with an express statement of which limitations apply to which category.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties (Seller: same caps and time limits as general)
- **Departure:** This contradicts a core playbook position: a separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why push back:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title or capacity fails, we have bought nothing, and capping recovery at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is commercially unacceptable.
- **Action:** Reject outright. This is non-negotiable.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance: Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("apply to all Claims of any nature")
- **Departure:** There is no fraud carve-out. As drafted, caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would apply to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Why push back:** The playbook requires these to be carved out of every limitation to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one on our side may waive this. "Any nature" combined with non-reliance is exactly the structure that would let the Seller argue fraud-based claims are contractually confined.
- **Action:** Insert a standalone clause: *nothing in clauses 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 or any other limitation limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers*. Also carve specific indemnities, title, tax and covenants out of "any nature."

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure: Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2
- **Departure:** The letter deems disclosed everything in the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." The playbook rejects all three.
- **Why push back:** This turns the warranties into a "find it yourself" regime and shifts the risk of every undisclosed problem onto us.
- **Action:**
  - Delete §1.1 and §1.2.
  - Require specific fair disclosure: each disclosure must be made against an identified warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
  - Data room documents may be incorporated only where specifically referenced in a specific disclosure.

**§1.4 (non-admission):** This is broadly acceptable as a no-admissions statement. We should add that nothing in it reduces the effect of a specific disclosure or qualifies any indemnity or fundamental warranty.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge: Clause 8.3
- **Departure:** This is a blanket exclusion covering:
  - actual knowledge of the Buyer and its advisers, and
  - constructive knowledge ("discoverable from the data room or public records").

  It is the widest possible form and goes further even than the general disclosure.
- **Why push back:** It would neutralise warranties on every issue our diligence identified, including the very items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) we are protecting through specific mechanisms. It also has no carve-out for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Action:** Delete. The playbook permits any knowledge qualifier only in the form of Seller-knowledge qualifiers on specific warranties, tied to named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent: Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Facts (DD-002, Disclosure §2):**
  - Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
  - Change-control consent is required under clause 11.2, with conditions in clause 11.3.
  - No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus deemed satisfaction "on delivery" of the written consent. The playbook rejects both: reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer, and consent-on-delivery ignores the 11.3 conditions.
- **Risk:** A consent whose conditions are never met may be ineffective. We could complete and then lose 30% of revenue.
- **Action:** Make it a condition precedent that requires both:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, and
  - documentary evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion.

  The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer. Also add a Seller obligation to keep us informed and not to agree to any change to Bluefen terms without our consent.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility: Clause 2 / 7
- **Facts (DD-003, Disclosure §3):**
  - About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
  - Change-control clause 8.1 and discharge clause 9.2.
  - Not repaid and no discharge as at 22 September.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers "a release to be provided following Completion." The playbook requires:
  - a current payout letter,
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, and
  - effective security releases at Completion.
- **Risk:** The deal is debt-free. Without release at Completion, the Company stays encumbered and change-control under 8.1 may be triggered.
- **Action:** Require all of the following:
  - a payout letter dated close to Completion, with a daily rate,
  - payment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds as a funds-flow line deducted from price,
  - signed releases and discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so do not offer it.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses: Funds flow / DD-005
- **Facts (Disclosure §5):**
  - AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses.
  - These are not in the funds flow.
  - On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and the like) are not addressed.
- **Departure:** The playbook says the funds flow must not silently exclude them. The Seller's own draft does exactly that, while calling them "a matter for the Seller." If they are a matter for the Seller, the funds flow must show it.
- **Risk:** The Company, now owned by us, pays AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion with no price adjustment.
- **Action:** Require one of:
  - a specific funds-flow line covering the bonuses plus all triggered on-costs, deducted from price (treated as Debt-like or a Transaction Expense), or
  - express Seller funding, backed by a specific indemnity.

  The Seller should also confirm the on-cost position in writing.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP: Clause 11.1
- **Facts (DD-004, DD-010, Disclosure §4):**
  - Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which is not bank-verified.
  - There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure:** The Seller's indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment." The playbook requires broadening it.
- **Why push back:** If title to the Project Materials has not passed, our loss is not limited to the AUD 180k fee. It could include infringement exposure, re-development cost, customer impact, and disputes over other SOWs or fees.
- **Action:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use Ironquay deliverables, and any Ironquay claim.
  - Keep a cure route: Seller procures payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees and delivers a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ideally make delivery of evidence of payment and the confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is either owed or paid. Ask for bank evidence either way.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident: Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
- **Facts (Disclosure §6):**
  - A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
  - The export may contain about 1,240 records.
  - Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Departure:** The cover note calls it "not expected to be material," which goes beyond the Seller's own disclosure. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed breach or put a dollar figure on it.
- **Action:** Require the Seller to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence,
  - complete the investigation (link-access logs, recipient confirmation, scope),
  - give us regular written updates and allow us to review any notification decision before Completion.

  Seek a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory, notification and third-party costs, outside the general cap and thresholds. The indemnity should not be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge. Reject any language characterising the incident as immaterial.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Facts (DD-008, DD-011, Disclosure §8):**
  - Three related renewals at AUD 110k each.
  - The disclosure is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Position:** Do not accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label. Equally, the playbook says not to classify these automatically as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- **Action:** Request the contracts, the timing of the renewal commitments relative to the locked-box or accounts date, termination rights, and the accrual status. The related-renewal pattern (three equal amounts read together) warrants checking whether they were entered or accelerated in contemplation of the sale. Decide on treatment (Debt-like, conduct-of-business covenant breach, or ordinary course) after assessment.

### 4.4 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime above." The playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **open**.
- **Action:** Reject the assertion that they are settled. Keep Tax (including a tax indemnity and longer limitation period) and IP as separate categories outside the general regime. Do not assume unlimited liability, and do not assume resolution either way.

### 4.5 Title: DD-012
- **Departure:** The Seller relies on its own share register. The Disclosure Letter (§10) concedes that the register is just "the source relied on" and that we have not verified it.
- **Action:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract,
  - PPSR search against the Seller and the Company,
  - original or certified share certificates,
  - share transfer and issue history,
  - constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption, drag and tag),
  - Seller board approval and authority,
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights to shares exist.

  Title must sit in the fundamental regime (see 1.4).

### 4.6 Lower-priority items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter says the lease imposes only a notification obligation and that the Mossvale clause restricts assignment rather than requiring consent to a share sale. These are not playbook issues, but they are Seller characterisations. Have the clauses reviewed to confirm there is no change-of-control trigger, and make any required lease notification a Completion deliverable.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (core playbook positions, no authorised fallback in play):**
1. Fundamental/Title under the general regime. Restore a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature." Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out. This is non-waivable.
3. Whole-data-room, Accounts, registers and public-records disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in clause 8.3. Delete it.
5. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" override. Delete it and keep the categories separate.
6. The assertion that Tax/IP are settled. Both remain open and separate.

**Restore our starting positions:**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft, which we do not have.
8. Thresholds: AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k tipping basket.
9. General claims period: 24 months. 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have.

**Completion protections:**
10. Bluefen: a condition precedent requiring both effective consent and evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
11. Riverlark: a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion.
12. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. Title: independent verification, not DD-012 alone.

**Specific indemnities and further diligence:**
14. Ironquay: a broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure, plus bank evidence on the AUD 180k.
15. DD-006: evidence preservation, investigation, regular updates and a specific indemnity. No characterisation as immaterial, and no assumption of breach.
16. Sandbar: obtain the documents and assess before deciding on treatment.
17. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the Seller's characterisation through clause review.

**Process:**
18. Respond in writing that no positions are agreed or final from the Buyer's side, and that "market standard" and "settled at principal level" statements are not accepted.
19. Request updated facts since 22 September 2026 on all open items.
20. Before any fallback is used, especially the 20% cap that the Seller has deliberately pitched at our fallback number, route it to Amelia Frost for written authority referencing this draft.

---

*Note: this review reflects the Seller's documents as supplied and our playbook. It is not a substitute for review of the full SPA text, which was not provided. Several clause references (e.g. 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) should be checked against the full draft once received.*

- **Departure:** Our position is 24 months. 18 months requires Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.
- **Hidden override:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" would quietly sweep title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants into the general regime. This breaches our rule that these categories stay separate.
- **Action:** Restore 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the blanket language and replace it with an express statement of which limitations apply to which category.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties (Seller: same caps and time limits as general)
- **Departure:** This contradicts a core playbook position: a separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Why push back:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title or capacity fails, we have bought nothing, and capping recovery at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is commercially unacceptable.
- **Action:** Reject outright. This is non-negotiable.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance: Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 ("apply to all Claims of any nature")
- **Departure:** There is no fraud carve-out. As drafted, caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance would apply to fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct.
- **Why push back:** The playbook requires these to be carved out of every limitation to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one on our side may waive this. "Any nature" combined with non-reliance is exactly the structure that would let the Seller argue fraud-based claims are contractually confined.
- **Action:** Insert a standalone clause: *nothing in clauses 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5 or any other limitation limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers, employees, agents or advisers*. Also carve specific indemnities, title, tax and covenants out of "any nature."

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure: Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2
- **Departure:** The letter deems disclosed everything in the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." The playbook rejects all three.
- **Why push back:** This turns the warranties into a "find it yourself" regime and shifts the risk of every undisclosed problem onto us.
- **Action:**
  - Delete §1.1 and §1.2.
  - Require specific fair disclosure: each disclosure must be made against an identified warranty, with enough detail for the Buyer to assess its nature and scope.
  - Data room documents may be incorporated only where specifically referenced in a specific disclosure.

**§1.4 (non-admission):** This is broadly acceptable as a no-admissions statement. We should add that nothing in it reduces the effect of a specific disclosure or qualifies any indemnity or fundamental warranty.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge: Clause 8.3
- **Departure:** This is a blanket exclusion covering:
  - actual knowledge of the Buyer and its advisers, and
  - constructive knowledge ("discoverable from the data room or public records").

  It is the widest possible form and goes further even than the general disclosure.
- **Why push back:** It would neutralise warranties on every issue our diligence identified, including the very items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) we are protecting through specific mechanisms. It also has no carve-out for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Action:** Delete. The playbook permits any knowledge qualifier only in the form of Seller-knowledge qualifiers on specific warranties, tied to named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. Buyer knowledge should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent: Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Facts (DD-002, Disclosure §2):**
  - Bluefen accounts for about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%.
  - Change-control consent is required under clause 11.2, with conditions in clause 11.3.
  - No final consent and no evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours plus deemed satisfaction "on delivery" of the written consent. The playbook rejects both: reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer, and consent-on-delivery ignores the 11.3 conditions.
- **Risk:** A consent whose conditions are never met may be ineffective. We could complete and then lose 30% of revenue.
- **Action:** Make it a condition precedent that requires both:
  - an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, and
  - documentary evidence, satisfactory to the Buyer, that every clause 11.3 condition is satisfied before Completion.

  The condition should be waivable only by the Buyer. Also add a Seller obligation to keep us informed and not to agree to any change to Bluefen terms without our consent.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility: Clause 2 / 7
- **Facts (DD-003, Disclosure §3):**
  - About AUD 3.2m outstanding.
  - Change-control clause 8.1 and discharge clause 9.2.
  - Not repaid and no discharge as at 22 September.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers "a release to be provided following Completion." The playbook requires:
  - a current payout letter,
  - direct repayment from Completion funds, and
  - effective security releases at Completion.
- **Risk:** The deal is debt-free. Without release at Completion, the Company stays encumbered and change-control under 8.1 may be triggered.
- **Action:** Require all of the following:
  - a payout letter dated close to Completion, with a daily rate,
  - payment directly to Riverlark from Completion funds as a funds-flow line deducted from price,
  - signed releases and discharges (including PPSR) delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so do not offer it.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses: Funds flow / DD-005
- **Facts (Disclosure §5):**
  - AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses.
  - These are not in the funds flow.
  - On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation and the like) are not addressed.
- **Departure:** The playbook says the funds flow must not silently exclude them. The Seller's own draft does exactly that, while calling them "a matter for the Seller." If they are a matter for the Seller, the funds flow must show it.
- **Risk:** The Company, now owned by us, pays AUD 420k plus on-costs after Completion with no price adjustment.
- **Action:** Require one of:
  - a specific funds-flow line covering the bonuses plus all triggered on-costs, deducted from price (treated as Debt-like or a Transaction Expense), or
  - express Seller funding, backed by a specific indemnity.

  The Seller should also confirm the on-cost position in writing.

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP: Clause 11.1
- **Facts (DD-004, DD-010, Disclosure §4):**
  - Transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee.
  - DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, which is not bank-verified.
  - There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure:** The Seller's indemnity covers only "the specific SOW3 payment." The playbook requires broadening it.
- **Why push back:** If title to the Project Materials has not passed, our loss is not limited to the AUD 180k fee. It could include infringement exposure, re-development cost, customer impact, and disputes over other SOWs or fees.
- **Action:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use Ironquay deliverables, and any Ironquay claim.
  - Keep a cure route: Seller procures payment of any outstanding SOW3 fees and delivers a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Ideally make delivery of evidence of payment and the confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is either owed or paid. Ask for bank evidence either way.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident: Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006
- **Facts (Disclosure §6):**
  - A download link was sent to an unintended external address.
  - The export may contain about 1,240 records.
  - Access, scope and notification duty are all unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Departure:** The cover note calls it "not expected to be material," which goes beyond the Seller's own disclosure. Equally, we should not treat it as a confirmed breach or put a dollar figure on it.
- **Action:** Require the Seller to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence,
  - complete the investigation (link-access logs, recipient confirmation, scope),
  - give us regular written updates and allow us to review any notification decision before Completion.

  Seek a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident, including regulatory, notification and third-party costs, outside the general cap and thresholds. The indemnity should not be qualified by disclosure or buyer knowledge. Reject any language characterising the incident as immaterial.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Facts (DD-008, DD-011, Disclosure §8):**
  - Three related renewals at AUD 110k each.
  - The disclosure is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Position:** Do not accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label. Equally, the playbook says not to classify these automatically as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- **Action:** Request the contracts, the timing of the renewal commitments relative to the locked-box or accounts date, termination rights, and the accrual status. The related-renewal pattern (three equal amounts read together) warrants checking whether they were entered or accelerated in contemplation of the sale. Decide on treatment (Debt-like, conduct-of-business covenant breach, or ordinary course) after assessment.

### 4.4 Tax and IP warranties
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime above." The playbook treats Tax and IP terms as **open**.
- **Action:** Reject the assertion that they are settled. Keep Tax (including a tax indemnity and longer limitation period) and IP as separate categories outside the general regime. Do not assume unlimited liability, and do not assume resolution either way.

### 4.5 Title: DD-012
- **Departure:** The Seller relies on its own share register. The Disclosure Letter (§10) concedes that the register is just "the source relied on" and that we have not verified it.
- **Action:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract,
  - PPSR search against the Seller and the Company,
  - original or certified share certificates,
  - share transfer and issue history,
  - constitution and any shareholder agreement (pre-emption, drag and tag),
  - Seller board approval and authority,
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or other rights to shares exist.

  Title must sit in the fundamental regime (see 1.4).

### 4.6 Lower-priority items: lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
The Disclosure Letter says the lease imposes only a notification obligation and that the Mossvale clause restricts assignment rather than requiring consent to a share sale. These are not playbook issues, but they are Seller characterisations. Have the clauses reviewed to confirm there is no change-of-control trigger, and make any required lease notification a Completion deliverable.

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright (core playbook positions, no authorised fallback in play):**
1. Fundamental/Title under the general regime. Restore a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and exclusion from the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
2. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature." Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out. This is non-waivable.
3. Whole-data-room, Accounts, registers and public-records disclosure. Require specific fair disclosure.
4. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion in clause 8.3. Delete it.
5. The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" override. Delete it and keep the categories separate.
6. The assertion that Tax/IP are settled. Both remain open and separate.

**Restore our starting positions:**
7. Cap: 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority for this draft, which we do not have.
8. Thresholds: AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k tipping basket.
9. General claims period: 24 months. 18 months only with Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have.

**Completion protections:**
10. Bluefen: a condition precedent requiring both effective consent and evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
11. Riverlark: a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion.
12. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
13. Title: independent verification, not DD-012 alone.

**Specific indemnities and further diligence:**
14. Ironquay: a broadened IP indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure, plus bank evidence on the AUD 180k.
15. DD-006: evidence preservation, investigation, regular updates and a specific indemnity. No characterisation as immaterial, and no assumption of breach.
16. Sandbar: obtain the documents and assess before deciding on treatment.
17. Lease and Mossvale: confirm the Seller's characterisation through clause review.

**Process:**
18. Respond in writing that no positions are agreed or final from the Buyer's side, and that "market standard" and "settled at principal level" statements are not accepted.
19. Request updated facts since 22 September 2026 on all open items.
20. Before any fallback is used, especially the 20% cap that the Seller has deliberately pitched at our fallback number, route it to Amelia Frost for written authority referencing this draft.
